paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יְרֻבַּ֜עַל ה֣וּא גִדְע֗וֹן וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עַל־עֵ֣ין חֲרֹ֑ד וּמַחֲנֵ֤ה מִדְיָן֙ הָיָה־ל֣וֹ מִצָּפ֔וֹן מִגִּבְעַ֥ת הַמּוֹרֶ֖ה בָּעֵֽמֶק׃

i18n.en: Then Yerubba'al, that is, Gid'on, and all the people who were with him rose early and encamped beside the spring of Charod; and the camp of Midyan was north of him, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.

notes.official: *yərubbaʿal hûʾ ḡiḏʿôn* 'Yerubba'al, that is, Gid'on': the narrator joins the name given in 6:32 to the hero's own name (`habbaal-baal-hebrew-bible-rendering-former-prophets`). 'Gid'on' = Gideon; 'Midyan' = Midian (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *ʿên ḥărōḏ* 'the spring of Charod' = Harod (ASV): the name echoes *ḥārēḏ* 'trembling' in v 3, where the fearful are sent home. *giḇʿaṯ hammôreh* 'the hill of Moreh', north of the spring across the Jezreel valley.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־גִּדְע֔וֹן רַ֗ב הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן בְּיָדָ֑ם פֶּן־יִתְפָּאֵ֨ר עָלַ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָדִ֖י הוֹשִׁ֥יעָה לִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Gid'on, "The people who are with you are too many for me to give Midyan into their hand, lest Yisra'el boast against me, saying, 'My own hand has saved me.'

notes.official: *rab hāʿām ... mittittî ʾeṯ-midyān bəyāḏām* 'The people ... are too many for me to give Midyan into their hand' (central `be-yedkhem-nittanu`). *pen-yiṯpāʾēr ʿālay yiśrāʾēl lēʾmōr yāḏî hôšîʿâ llî* 'lest Yisra'el boast against me, saying, "My own hand has saved me"': the reduction of the army in vv 2-8 is motivated theologically. Victory must be seen as YHWH's.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְרָ֨א נָ֜א בְּאָזְנֵ֤י הָעָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מִֽי־יָרֵ֣א וְחָרֵ֔ד יָשֹׁ֥ב וְיִצְפֹּ֖ר מֵהַ֣ר הַגִּלְעָ֑ד וַיָּ֣שָׁב מִן־הָעָ֗ם עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔לֶף וַעֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים נִשְׁאָֽרוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Now therefore, proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, 'Whoever is fearful and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gil'ad.'" And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

notes.official: *mî-yārēʾ wəḥārēḏ* 'Whoever is fearful and trembling': the exemption of the fearful is the law of Deut 20:8. *yāšōḇ wəyiṣpōr mēhar haggilʿāḏ* 'let him turn back and depart from Mount Gil'ad' has two difficulties (overlay `lexical-cruxes-judges-7`). The verb *ṣāp̄ar* is not otherwise attested in this sense; the KJV's 'depart early' derives it from *ṣəp̄îrâ* 'morning' (the ASV has only 'depart'), and others render 'turn back' or 'circle round'. And Gil'ad lies east of the Jordan, while Gid'on is camped west of it by the spring of Charod, so many commentators emend to 'Mount Gilboa', the range above the spring (Boling, *Judges*, AB 6A, 1975; Webb, *The Book of Judges*, NICOT, 2012). The line translates the MT (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). Of 32,000, 22,000 leave.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־גִּדְע֗וֹן עוֹד֮ הָעָ֣ם רָב֒ הוֹרֵ֤ד אוֹתָם֙ אֶל־הַמַּ֔יִם וְאֶצְרְפֶ֥נּוּ לְךָ֖ שָׁ֑ם וְהָיָ֡ה אֲשֶׁר֩ אֹמַ֨ר אֵלֶ֜יךָ זֶ֣ה ׀ יֵלֵ֣ךְ אִתָּ֗ךְ ה֚וּא יֵלֵ֣ךְ אִתָּ֔ךְ וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁר־אֹמַ֜ר אֵלֶ֗יךָ זֶ֚ה לֹא־יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֔ךְ ה֖וּא לֹ֥א יֵלֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Gid'on, "The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and I will test them for you there; and it shall be that of whom I say to you, 'This one shall go with you,' he shall go with you; and of whomever I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you,' he shall not go."

notes.official: *wəʾeṣrəp̄ennû ləḵā šām* 'and I will test them for you there': *ṣārap̄* is the smelter's verb, 'refine', used of the testing of people (Isa 48:10; Zech 13:9). The quoted formulas 'This one shall go with you' are in single marks.

paragraphs.text: וַיּ֥וֹרֶד אֶת־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־הַמָּ֑יִם (ס) וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־גִּדְע֗וֹן כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יָלֹק֩ בִּלְשׁוֹנ֨וֹ מִן־הַמַּ֜יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר יָלֹ֣ק הַכֶּ֗לֶב תַּצִּ֤יג אוֹתוֹ֙ לְבָ֔ד וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִכְרַ֥ע עַל־בִּרְכָּ֖יו לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: So he brought the people down to the water; and YHWH said to Gid'on, "Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you shall set him by himself; and so everyone who kneels down on his knees to drink."

notes.official: *wayyôreḏ ʾeṯ-hāʿām ʾel-hammāyim* 'So he brought the people down to the water': the source marks a *setumah* (ס) after this clause, inside the verse, which is kept in the Hebrew field (central `piska-b-emtza-pasuq-masoretic-paragraph-break`); the English line makes no break. *kōl ʾăšer-yālōq bilšônô min-hammayim kaʾăšer yālōq hakkeleḇ* 'Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps' is set apart from 'everyone who kneels down on his knees to drink'. The narrative does not explain why the lappers are chosen, and the explanations (alertness, or simply a sorting device that leaves the smallest group) are later.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִסְפַּ֞ר הַֽמֲלַקְקִ֤ים בְּיָדָם֙ אֶל־פִּיהֶ֔ם שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וְכֹל֙ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם כָּרְע֥וּ עַל־בִּרְכֵיהֶ֖ם לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מָֽיִם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the number of those who lapped, with their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; and all the rest of the people knelt down on their knees to drink water.

notes.official: *mispar hamalaqqəqîm bəyāḏām ʾel-pîhem* 'the number of those who lapped, with their hand to their mouth': in the MT the phrase stands with the lappers, although v 5 describes lapping 'with the tongue, as a dog laps'. Some LXX witnesses and many commentators transfer it to the kneelers, who would then drink from their hands. The line keeps the MT placement (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-judges-7`): read with the MT, the lappers bring the water to the mouth by hand and then lap it.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־גִּדְע֗וֹן בִּשְׁלֹשׁ֩ מֵא֨וֹת הָאִ֤ישׁ הַֽמֲלַקְקִים֙ אוֹשִׁ֣יעַ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְכָל־הָעָ֔ם יֵלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Gid'on, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and give Midyan into your hand; and let all the people go, each man to his place."

notes.official: *bišlōš mēʾôṯ hāʾîš hamalaqqəqîm ʾôšîaʿ ʾeṯkem* 'By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you' (central `be-yedkhem-nittanu`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶת־צֵדָה֩ הָעָ֨ם בְּיָדָ֜ם וְאֵ֣ת שׁוֹפְרֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שִׁלַּח֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְאֹֽהָלָ֔יו וּבִשְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת הָאִ֖ישׁ הֶֽחֱזִ֑יק וּמַחֲנֵ֣ה מִדְיָ֔ן הָ֥יָה ל֖וֹ מִתַּ֥חַת בָּעֵֽמֶק׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So the people took provisions in their hand, and their shofars; and he sent all the men of Yisra'el away, each man to his tents, but kept the three hundred men; and the camp of Midyan was below him in the valley.

notes.official: *wayyiqḥû ʾeṯ-ṣēḏâ hāʿām bəyāḏām wəʾēṯ šôp̄ərōṯêhem* 'So the people took provisions in their hand, and their shofars': the syntax is awkward (object marker before *ṣēḏâ*, subject after it), and many emend to *ʾeṯ-kaddê hāʿām* 'the jars of the people', which anticipates the jars of v 16. The line translates the MT (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-judges-7`; ASV 'victuals'). 'shofars' (central `shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus`): the 300 keep the horns of the departing men, so each has one (v 16). *wəʾēṯ kol-ʾîš yiśrāʾēl šillaḥ ʾîš ləʾōhālāyw* 'and he sent all the men of Yisra'el away, each man to his tents'.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה ק֖וּם רֵ֣ד בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כִּ֥י נְתַתִּ֖יו בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass that same night that YHWH said to him, "Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

notes.official: *qûm rēḏ bammaḥăneh kî nəṯattîw bəyāḏeḵā* 'Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand' (central `be-yedkhem-nittanu`): the perfect *nəṯattîw* states the outcome as already accomplished.

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־יָרֵ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לָרֶ֑דֶת רֵ֥ד אַתָּ֛ה וּפֻרָ֥ה נַעַרְךָ֖ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp, you and Purah your attendant,

notes.official: 'Purah' identical in both forms. *naʿarəḵā* 'your attendant' (ASV 'thy servant'), the armour-bearer or squire.

paragraphs.text: וְשָֽׁמַעְתָּ֙ מַה־יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ וְאַחַר֙ תֶּחֱזַ֣קְנָה יָדֶ֔יךָ וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֵּ֤רֶד הוּא֙ וּפֻרָ֣ה נַעֲר֔וֹ אֶל־קְצֵ֥ה הַחֲמֻשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: and you shall hear what they say; and afterward your hands shall be strengthened, and you shall go down against the camp." Then he went down with Purah his attendant to the outskirts of the armed men who were in the camp.

notes.official: *wəʾaḥar teḥĕzaqnâ yāḏeyḵā* 'and afterward your hands shall be strengthened'. *ʾel-qəṣēh haḥămušîm* 'to the outskirts of the armed men': *ḥămušîm* is the term for troops in battle order (Ex 13:18; Josh 1:14; 4:12; ASV 'armed men').

paragraphs.text: וּמִדְיָ֨ן וַעֲמָלֵ֤ק וְכָל־בְּנֵי־קֶ֙דֶם֙ נֹפְלִ֣ים בָּעֵ֔מֶק כָּאַרְבֶּ֖ה לָרֹ֑ב וְלִגְמַלֵּיהֶם֙ אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֔ר כַּח֛וֹל שֶׁעַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And Midyan and Amaleq and all the children of the east lay along the valley like locusts in multitude; and their camels were without number, as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude.

notes.official: 'Amaleq' = Amalek (central `amalek-perennial-enemy-ex-17-deut-25-1-sam-15-esther-cross-corpus`). *kol-bənê-qeḏem* 'all the children of the east' (as Judg 6:3, 33). *kāʾarbeh lārōḇ* 'like locusts in multitude' and *kaḥôl šeʿal-śəp̄aṯ hayyām* 'as the sand that is on the seashore' are the stock similes of numberless hosts (Judg 6:5; Josh 11:4).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א גִדְע֔וֹן וְהִ֨נֵּה־אִ֔ישׁ מְסַפֵּ֥ר לְרֵעֵ֖הוּ חֲל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הִנֵּ֧ה חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֗מְתִּי וְהִנֵּ֨ה צלול [צְלִ֜יל] לֶ֤חֶם שְׂעֹרִים֙ מִתְהַפֵּךְ֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה מִדְיָ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֣א עַד־הָ֠אֹהֶל וַיַּכֵּ֧הוּ וַיִּפֹּ֛ל וַיַּהַפְכֵ֥הוּ לְמַ֖עְלָה וְנָפַ֥ל הָאֹֽהֶל׃

i18n.en: And Gid'on came, and behold, a man was telling a dream to his companion; and he said, "Behold, I dreamed a dream, and behold, a round loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midyan; and it came to the tent and struck it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, and the tent lay flat."

notes.official: *wəhinnēh ṣəlîl leḥem śəʿōrîm miṯhappēḵ bəmaḥănēh miḏyān* 'and behold, a round loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midyan': the Ketiv *ṣlwl* and the Qere *ṣəlîl* differ in spelling only, and the word occurs nowhere else; 'a round loaf' (ASV 'a cake') follows the context and the versions (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-judges-7`). Barley bread was the food of the poor and the farmer, and the dream sets the farmers of Israel against the tents of the nomad camp. *wənāp̄al hāʾōhel* 'and the tent lay flat'.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨עַן רֵעֵ֤הוּ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ין זֹ֔את בִּלְתִּ֗י אִם־חֶ֛רֶב גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָ֖שׁ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נָתַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־מִדְיָ֖ן וְאֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And his companion answered and said, "This is nothing else but the sword of Gid'on the son of Yo'ash, a man of Yisra'el; into his hand the Elohim has given Midyan and all the camp."

notes.official: *ʾên zōʾṯ biltî ʾim-ḥereḇ giḏʿôn ben-yôʾāš* 'This is nothing else but the sword of Gid'on the son of Yo'ash' (Joash). *nāṯan hāʾĕlōhîm bəyāḏô ʾeṯ-miḏyān* 'into his hand the Elohim has given Midyan' (central `be-yedkhem-nittanu`): the Hebrew has the article, and the line prints 'the Elohim' under `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`, clause 1. The speaker is a Midyanite, but the narrator presents the dream as the sign YHWH promised Gid'on (vv 9-11), and the deity named is the one who gives Midyan into his hand. The same holds for the Pelishti speech of 1 Sam 5:7, which the corpus prints with a capital.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ גִּדְע֜וֹן אֶת־מִסְפַּ֧ר הַחֲל֛וֹם וְאֶת־שִׁבְר֖וֹ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ אֶל־מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ק֔וּמוּ כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּיֶדְכֶ֖ם אֶת־מַחֲנֵ֥ה מִדְיָֽן׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Gid'on heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he bowed down; and he returned to the camp of Yisra'el and said, "Arise, for YHWH has given the camp of Midyan into your hand."

notes.official: *ʾeṯ-mispar haḥălôm wəʾeṯ-šiḇrô* 'the telling of the dream and its interpretation': *šeḇer* 'breaking' is used for the interpretation of a dream only here, from the root 'break, solve'. *wayyištāḥû* 'he bowed down' (central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship`, Former Prophets clause; ASV 'worshipped'). *qûmû kî-nāṯan YHWH bəyeḏḵem ʾeṯ-maḥănēh miḏyān* 'Arise, for YHWH has given the camp of Midyan into your hand' (central `be-yedkhem-nittanu`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֛חַץ אֶת־שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת הָאִ֖ישׁ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שׁוֹפָר֤וֹת בְּיַד־כֻּלָּם֙ וְכַדִּ֣ים רֵקִ֔ים וְלַפִּדִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ הַכַּדִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put shofars into the hands of all of them, and empty jars, with torches inside the jars.

notes.official: *wayyaḥaṣ ... šəlōšâ rāʾšîm* 'he divided ... into three companies' (literally 'heads'). *šôp̄ārôṯ ... wəḵaddîm rēqîm wəlappiḏîm bəṯôḵ hakkaddîm* 'shofars ... and empty jars, with torches inside the jars' (central `shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus`). The jars hide the torches until the moment of attack.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מִמֶּ֥נִּי תִרְא֖וּ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֥י בָא֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה כַאֲשֶׁר־אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה כֵּ֥ן תַּעֲשֽׂוּן׃

i18n.en: And he said to them, "Watch me and do likewise; and behold, when I come to the outskirts of the camp, it shall be that as I do, so you shall do.

notes.official: *mimmennî tirʾû wəḵēn taʿăśû* 'Watch me and do likewise'.

paragraphs.text: וְתָקַעְתִּי֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר אָנֹכִ֖י וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתִּ֑י וּתְקַעְתֶּ֨ם בַּשּׁוֹפָר֜וֹת גַּם־אַתֶּ֗ם סְבִיבוֹת֙ כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם לַיהוָ֥ה וּלְגִדְעֽוֹן׃ (פ)

i18n.en: When I blow the shofar, I and all who are with me, then you also shall blow the shofars all around the whole camp and say, 'For YHWH and for Gid'on!'"

notes.official: *wəṯāqaʿtî baššôp̄ār* 'When I blow the shofar': *tāqaʿ* is the verb for blowing a horn, as in Josh 6 (central `shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus`). *laYHWH ûləḡiḏʿôn* 'For YHWH and for Gid'on!': the watchword, which v 20 repeats with 'a sword'. Gid'on's command contains the watchword in single marks.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א גִ֠דְעוֹן וּמֵאָה־אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֜וֹ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה רֹ֚אשׁ הָאַשְׁמֹ֣רֶת הַתִּֽיכוֹנָ֔ה אַ֛ךְ הָקֵ֥ם הֵקִ֖ימוּ אֶת־הַשֹּֽׁמְרִ֑ים וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁ֣וֹפָר֔וֹת וְנָפ֥וֹץ הַכַּדִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּיָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: So Gid'on and the hundred men who were with him came to the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just posted the watchmen; and they blew the shofars and smashed the jars that were in their hands.

notes.official: *rōʾš hāʾašmōreṯ hattîḵônâ* 'at the beginning of the middle watch': the night is divided into three watches (Lam 2:19; Ex 14:24 'the morning watch'). The attack comes shortly after the change of sentries (*hāqēm hēqîmû ʾeṯ-haššōmərîm* 'when they had just posted the watchmen'). *wənāp̄ôṣ hakkaddîm* 'and smashed the jars'.

paragraphs.text: וַֽ֠יִּתְקְעוּ שְׁלֹ֨שֶׁת הָרָאשִׁ֥ים בַּשּֽׁוֹפָרוֹת֮ וַיִּשְׁבְּר֣וּ הַכַּדִּים֒ וַיַּחֲזִ֤יקוּ בְיַד־שְׂמאוֹלָם֙ בַּלַּפִּדִ֔ים וּבְיַ֨ד־יְמִינָ֔ם הַשּׁוֹפָר֖וֹת לִתְק֑וֹעַ וַֽיִּקְרְא֔וּ חֶ֥רֶב לַֽיהוָ֖ה וּלְגִדְעֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And the three companies blew the shofars and broke the jars, and held the torches in their left hands and the shofars in their right hands to blow; and they cried, "A sword for YHWH and for Gid'on!"

notes.official: *wayyiṯqəʿû šəlōšeṯ hārāʾšîm baššôp̄ārôṯ* 'And the three companies blew the shofars'. Each man has a torch in his left hand and a shofar in his right, which leaves no hand for a sword: the battle cry names a sword, but YHWH fights it (v 22). *ḥereḇ laYHWH ûləḡiḏʿôn* 'A sword for YHWH and for Gid'on!': the cry repeats the watchword of v 18 (*laYHWH ûləḡiḏʿôn* 'For YHWH and for Gid'on!') with the same preposition *lə-* and adds 'sword'. The line therefore renders the preposition as in v 18 (NRSV, NJPS), where the ASV has a possessive, 'The sword of Jehovah and of Gideon' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-judges-7`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֔יו סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיָּ֧רָץ כָּל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה וַיָּרִ֖יעוּ ויניסו [וַיָּנֽוּסוּ׃]

i18n.en: And they stood each man in his place around the camp; and all the camp ran, and they shouted and fled.

notes.official: *wayyaʿamḏû ʾîš taḥtāyw* 'And they stood each man in his place': the 300 do not attack, and the rout is the enemy's own. *wayyārāṣ kol-hammaḥăneh wayyārîʿû wayyānûsû* 'and all the camp ran, and they shouted and fled': the subject is the Midyanite camp. The Ketiv *wyynysw* is a Hiphil, 'and they put to flight' (followed by the ASV, 'and put them to flight'), and the Qere *wayyānûsû* is a Qal, 'and they fled'. The line translates the Qere (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֮ שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת֒ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ת חֶ֥רֶב אִ֛ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֖הוּ וּבְכָל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיָּ֨נָס הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה עַד־בֵּ֤ית הַשִּׁטָּה֙ צְֽרֵרָ֔תָה עַ֛ד שְׂפַת־אָבֵ֥ל מְחוֹלָ֖ה עַל־טַבָּֽת׃

i18n.en: And they blew the three hundred shofars, and YHWH set every man's sword against his companion, even throughout all the camp; and the camp fled as far as Beit-haShittah toward Tzererah, as far as the border of Avel-Mecholah, by Tabbat.

notes.official:
*wayyiṯqəʿû šəlōš-mēʾôṯ haššôp̄ārôṯ* 'And they blew the three hundred shofars' (central `shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus`). *wayyāśem YHWH ʾēṯ ḥereḇ ʾîš bərēʿēhû ûḇəḵol-hammaḥăneh* 'and YHWH set every man's sword against his companion, even throughout all the camp': the panic in which an army turns on itself is a motif of YHWH's wars (1 Sam 14:20; 2 Chr 20:23; Ezek 38:21). 'Beit-haShittah' = Beth-shittah; 'Tzererah' = Zererah; 'Avel-Mecholah' = Abel-meholah; 'Tabbat' = Tabbath (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). The flight runs south-east toward the Jordan.

*šôp̄ār* is 'shofar' in every context under the central entry. 'trumpet' is reserved for the metal *ḥăṣōṣərâ*, so the line differs from the ASV and from the canon's English, which both say 'trumpets'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) reads Judges 7 as a whole: 'the 300 men who surround an enemy camp with «trumpets» and sound them all together to drive the men mad use instruments emitting greatly amplified ultrasound … Indeed, the encircled people goes mad, the soldiers kill one another and take flight.' The canon's 'kill one another' corresponds to this verse. The line renders *šôp̄ār* as the ram's horn and the verb *śîm* ('set') literally, and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּצָּעֵ֧ק אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מִנַּפְתָּלִ֥י וּמִן־אָשֵׁ֖ר וּמִן־כָּל־מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן׃

i18n.en: And the men of Yisra'el were called out from Naftali and from Asher and from all Menasheh, and they pursued Midyan.

notes.official: *wayyiṣṣāʿēq ʾîš-yiśrāʾēl* 'And the men of Yisra'el were called out': the tribes summoned in 6:35 now join the pursuit. 'Naftali' = Naphtali; 'Menasheh' = Manasseh; 'Asher' identical.

paragraphs.text: וּמַלְאָכִ֡ים שָׁלַ֣ח גִּדְעוֹן֩ בְּכָל־הַ֨ר אֶפְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר רְד֞וּ לִקְרַ֤את מִדְיָן֙ וְלִכְד֤וּ לָהֶם֙ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֛ד בֵּ֥ית בָּרָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וַיִּצָּעֵ֞ק כָּל־אִ֤ישׁ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּ אֶת־הַמַּ֔יִם עַ֛ד בֵּ֥ית בָּרָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And Gid'on sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Efrayim, saying, "Come down against Midyan, and seize the waters before them as far as Beit-Barah, and the Yarden." So all the men of Efrayim were called out, and they seized the waters as far as Beit-Barah, and the Yarden.

notes.official: *wəliḵdû lāhem ʾeṯ-hammayim* 'and seize the waters': the fords of the Jordan, to cut off the retreat (cf. 3:28; 12:5). 'Efrayim' = Ephraim; 'Beit-Barah' = Beth-barah (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֡וּ שְׁנֵֽי־שָׂרֵ֨י מִדְיָ֜ן אֶת־עֹרֵ֣ב וְאֶת־זְאֵ֗ב וַיַּהַרְג֨וּ אֶת־עוֹרֵ֤ב בְּצוּר־עוֹרֵב֙ וְאֶת־זְאֵב֙ הָרְג֣וּ בְיֶֽקֶב־זְאֵ֔ב וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אֶל־מִדְיָ֑ן וְרֹאשׁ־עֹרֵ֣ב וּזְאֵ֔ב הֵבִ֙יאוּ֙ אֶל־גִּדְע֔וֹן מֵעֵ֖בֶר לַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And they captured the two captains of Midyan, Orev and Ze'ev; and they killed Orev at the rock of Orev, and Ze'ev they killed at the winepress of Ze'ev; and they pursued Midyan; and they brought the heads of Orev and Ze'ev to Gid'on beyond the Yarden.

notes.official: *šənê-śārê miḏyān ʾeṯ-ʿōrēḇ wəʾeṯ-zəʾēḇ* 'the two captains of Midyan, Orev and Ze'ev' = Oreb and Zeeb (ASV 'the two princes of Midian'). *śar* is the general word for an official or commander, as in 'captain of the host' (Josh 5:14); the two are war leaders, not royal sons, so 'captains' replaces the ASV's 'princes' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-judges-7`; NRSV 'captains'). The names mean 'raven' and 'wolf'. *bəṣûr-ʿôrēḇ ... bəyeqeḇ-zəʾēḇ* 'at the rock of Orev ... at the winepress of Ze'ev' are translated as descriptive toponyms (ASV), as the names convention does for *giḇʿaṯ hāʿărālôṯ* (Josh 5:3). The victory is remembered as 'the day of Midian' (Isa 9:3; 10:26; Ps 83:12).
